en: The Sūtra of the Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī Spoken by the Buddha,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court Dispersing Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
and Great Master of Enlightened Teaching, Dharma-bhadra, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the buddha-field of Sukhāvatī,
together with a great assembly of bodhisattvas and a multitude of bhūtas.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara came to where the Buddha was;
having arrived, he prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet and sat to one side.
There was also another Bodhisattva Mahāsattva named Mañjuśrī.
He also went to where the Buddha was; having arrived, he circumambulated the Buddha three times, prostrated with his head at the Buddha’s feet, and withdrew to sit to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One, having seen the Bodhisattva Mahāśrī, [spoke].
He addressed the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara, saying:
"This Bodhisattva Mahāmaṅgala possesses a dhāraṇī.
If, within this turbid and evil world of Jambudvīpa..."
There are bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās who see, hear, rejoice in,
read, recite, receive, and uphold this Dharma;
they believe and understand it, contemplate it, and keep it in mind.
Those who are poor and suffering shall attain great wealth and nobility;
even the bhūtas will all be made to love and revere them.
Such merits as these cannot be fully described.
At that time, having heard the Buddha’s words,
the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara was filled with joy and exultation; he immediately rose from his seat,
joined his palms, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One, I now wish to hear it;
I only pray that the World-Honored One will proclaim it for me.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke the Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā: locami śrīpadmini dhānadi-patti auḥ mahāyaśe padmanittri maḥ.
Haya-ni-ṭi ānandaye ratna-prabhā maheśvari kṛti-kṛti sarva-arghāya.
dvau śloṃ 13 tiṇi tiṇi 14 si si si si 15 niṭi niṭi 16 heṇi heṇi 17 ālakṣami 18 miṇaśaya 19 sarvalakṣami miśraṇaya 20.
*Svāhā* (20). *Namo sarvabuddhabodhisattvebhyaḥ svāhā* (21–22).
At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this sutra, [remained silent].
Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, Mahāmaṅgala Bodhisattva,
and all the bodhisattvas and hosts of bhūtas,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly delighted; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sutra Spoken by the Buddha on the Great Auspicious Dhāraṇī.
